title: Ship TypeScript RAG + agent quickstart template (streaming, retries, OTel instrumentation)
creator: Monica Patel
body:
## Context
We’re shipping a production-minded RAG + agent template for TypeScript that mirrors the Python template capabilities and Redwood’s recommended operational hooks. This is one of the v1 templates used for onboarding PLG engineers and as a reference implementation for platform teams.

This ticket covers the TypeScript template end-to-end: scaffold, streaming robustness, timeout/retry defaults, provider abstraction (Redwood API first), tool-calling agent loop with guardrails, baseline RAG retrieval pipeline, and required observability instrumentation (OTel traces/metrics + structured logs + correlation IDs).

## Goals
- Provide a TypeScript template that can be scaffolded via GitHub template repo and CLI and can reach “first success” quickly.
- Ensure safe defaults: timeouts, retries/backoff, max token/cost controls, tool guardrails.
- Ensure production-grade observability: traces + metrics + logs that match Redwood conventions and are usable in Redwood Console and the observability pack dashboards.
- Keep vendor lock-in minimal: provider wrapper pattern and configuration via env vars.

## Non-goals
- Full hosted vector DB integrations beyond a placeholder adapter interface (keep scope tight for v1).
- Complex multi-agent orchestration beyond a single-loop tool-calling agent with max-iterations guard.
- Shipping an opinionated front-end UI (this template is API/server-first).

## Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
### Template behavior
- `npm install && npm run dev` works with minimal setup (after setting env vars).
- Implements RAG pipeline:
  - document ingest/chunk (simple defaults)
  - embedding + index interface
  - retriever returns top-k chunks with scores
  - prompt assembly includes citations/source IDs
- Implements agent loop:
  - tool schema validation and tool output size limits
  - max tool iterations (default 5) with clear error on exceed
  - tool errors are captured, logged with taxonomy, and surfaced to the model as tool failure messages (without leaking secrets)

### Streaming + resilience
- Streaming responses are robust to transient network disconnects:
  - request timeout defaults align with safe-defaults policy
  - retry/backoff for idempotent operations; streaming retry strategy must avoid duplicating user-visible output (documented behavior)
  - explicit handling for “stream ended unexpectedly” and partial response
- Retry policy:
  - exponential backoff with jitter
  - max attempts configured via env
  - do not retry on auth/validation errors (401/403/4xx non-429)

### Observability (required)
- Traces emitted via OpenTelemetry with a minimum viable span hierarchy:
  - `http.server` span for inbound request
  - `redwood.llm` span for model call
  - `rag.retrieve` span
  - `agent.loop` span with child spans per tool invocation `tool.<name>`
- Standard span attributes and log fields:
  - `redwood.request_id` (propagated into logs/traces)
  - model name + pinned version string
  - token usage fields (when available), latency breakdown, and error category
- Metrics:
  - request latency and status
  - tool error rate
  - retrieval hit/empty rate
  - token counts and estimated cost (best-effort; no high-cardinality labels)
- Redaction defaults:
  - do not log prompt/user content by default
  - include guidance and a safe toggle for debug logging (clearly marked “do not enable in prod”)

### Docs / ergonomics
- README follows standardized structure (setup, run, verify observability, troubleshooting, cost controls).
- Links to docs walkthrough and troubleshooting pages.
- Template must support Hosted by default; include notes for Dedicated/Private (networking/collector endpoints).

## Implementation notes
- Runtime: Node 20+.
- Server: lightweight (Express/Fastify acceptable). Avoid heavy framework coupling.
- Provider abstraction:
  - `LLMClient` wrapper that can target Redwood API first; optional OpenAI-compat mode if configured.
  - Ensure model pinning is explicit (`MODEL` env var required; no “latest” implicit default in prod config).
- Config:
  - `dotenv` for local dev only; production relies on env injection.
  - Validation at boot with clear messages; `doctor` command will validate as part of ENG-4185.

## Concrete work items
1) Scaffold template repo structure (mirroring Python where reasonable)
- `src/server.ts`, `src/agent/*`, `src/rag/*`, `src/observability/*`, `src/config.ts`
- `scripts/` for smoke tests / verification
- `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose` for local OTel collector (coordinated with ENG-4184)

2) Streaming chat endpoint
- `/chat` endpoint supports streaming responses to client
- Graceful handling of client disconnect and upstream stream interruption

3) Retry/timeout defaults
- Centralized HTTP client wrapper with retry and timeout
- Document the “streaming reconnect” behavior and limitations

4) OTel + structured logs
- OTel SDK initialization with resource attributes
- Span naming and attributes aligned to conventions
- Structured JSON logs with correlation ID + error taxonomy

5) Tool-calling agent loop
- Basic tools:
  - `search_documents(query)` -> uses retriever
  - `get_document(id)` -> returns chunk(s) with size cap
- Tool schema validation + error handling

6) RAG baseline
- Local in-memory / file-backed index option for v1 (simple, deterministic)
- Retriever interface + adapter hook for future hosted vector DB

7) CI checks and smoke tests
- Hook into ENG-4186 for streaming/tool smoke tests; ensure this template is included.

## Links / Related artifacts
- Confluence requirements: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/template-requirements-rag-agents
- Observability standard: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/observability-hooks-standard
- Safe defaults policy: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/safe-defaults-and-guardrails
- Docs walkthrough (draft): redwood-docs PR-842
- Troubleshooting page: redwood-docs PR-843
- Observability reference: redwood-docs PR-844

## GitHub PRs
- redwood-quickstarts PR-108: Add TypeScript template scaffold (merged)
- redwood-quickstarts PR-109: Structured output + tool schema validation patterns (merged)
- redwood-sdk-typescript PR-488: Streaming reconnect + better error types (merged; required for robust template streaming)
- redwood-sdk-typescript PR-489: OTel-friendly hooks/middleware points (merged)

## Security / Privacy checklist
- [x] No secrets in repo; `.env.example` only
- [x] Logging redaction on by default; docs call out how to safely enable debug
- [x] Dependency pinning aligned with template policy (tracked in ENG-4190)
- [x] Telemetry tagging headers are opt-in due to corporate proxy issues; defaults off

## Rollout notes
- Ship as part of internal beta first, then public docs link once smoke tests are stable.
- Coordinate with Observability Pack dashboards so users can immediately validate emitted signals.

## Open questions (resolved)
- Telemetry header for adoption metrics: make opt-in via env (`TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true`) to avoid proxy 4xx issues.
- High-cardinality attributes: avoid `user_id`/`session_id` tags; allow correlation via request id only.

## Definition of Done
- Template passes CI + streaming/tool smoke tests
- README standardized and reviewed by Docs
- OTel spans/metrics visible in local collector with provided docker-compose
- Security review nits addressed (no prompt logging by default, redaction verified)
comments: 2025-02-14 (Dana Lo): Initial scaffold in progress. Aligning folder layout with Python template but keeping Node entrypoints minimal. Will target Fastify for simple streaming + middleware, unless Express ends up easier for SSE.

2025-02-19 (Allison Grant): Please ensure span attributes follow the quickstart tracing conventions and avoid high-cardinality tags. In particular, do not attach raw tool args or retrieved text to spans/logs by default. Request ID propagation is mandatory.

2025-02-21 (Ibrahim Khan): Streaming resilience: do not silently retry mid-stream in a way that duplicates user-visible tokens. If reconnect happens, surface a partial response + retry suggestion. SDK PR-488 should provide better error typing; template should map errors into taxonomy categories.
2025-02-26 (Dana Lo): PR-108 opened with scaffold + basic streaming endpoint. Next up: tool schema validation and structured output parsing (PR-109).

2025-03-03 (Monica Patel): Please add explicit config validation at boot (missing API key/model should fail fast with actionable error). Also make telemetry tags opt-in; we’re seeing proxies reject unknown headers in internal beta.

2025-03-07 (Dana Lo): Merged PR-109. Tool schema failures now produce `TEMPLATE_TOOL_SCHEMA_ERROR` with remediation text and logs include `redwood.request_id`. Added max-iterations guard (default 5) and tool output size cap (64KB).

2025-03-11 (Sahana Iyer): Added this template to the smoke-test matrix for ENG-4186. We had some flakiness around SSE disconnect; mitigation: longer test timeout + retry the test job (not the app) and isolate ports per job.

2025-03-14 (Elliot Price): README structure looks good. Please add a short “Verify observability” section showing how to confirm traces reach the local collector and where the request id appears. Also add a link to the troubleshooting doc for 401/429/timeouts.

2025-03-18 (Dana Lo): Marking done. Template is working end-to-end: RAG retrieve span, agent loop spans, structured logs + redaction defaults, streaming endpoint stable in CI. Telemetry header/tags are opt-in via env to avoid proxy 4xx.
